title: Lower-Capacity Relations in Transistor Correlation Attacks
summary: With known whitening output, all optimal trails require at least about two to the power 31.5 keystream blocks; whether lower-capacity relations raise capacity and reduce data needs remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the multiple-linear-approximation correlation attack on Transistor, an information-theoretic analysis that assumes the whitening LFSR output is known estimates that using all optimal linear trails requires at least about $2^{31.5}$ keystream blocks. This estimate assumes, without establishing, that adding linear relations of lower capacity cannot improve the attack. Determine whether such additional relations increase the combined capacity and, if so, derive the resulting minimum keystream data complexity under the same known-whitening-output model.

scope.domain: The problem concerns linear cryptanalysis of the Transistor stream cipher using a multiple-linear-approximation correlation attack.
assumptions: The whitening LFSR output is known to the attacker.
The existing estimate assumes that additional lower-capacity linear relations cannot improve the attack.
parameters: Linear trails and relations included in the attack, which determine the combined capacity
Keystream blocks, which measure the attack's data complexity
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether additional lower-capacity relations increase the combined capacity and, if so, derive the resulting minimum keystream data complexity under the known-whitening-output model.

progress.summary: The paper gives an information-theoretic estimate of at least about two to the power 31.5 keystream blocks for all optimal trails under known whitening output. It treats non-improvement from lower-capacity relations as an assumption rather than establishing it.
citation_labels: Jules Baudrin et al., Transistor: a TFHE-friendly Stream Cipher
